clue.text: Order evoking cries of " chin-chin *"?

parts.note: ordering a large measure of spirits at the bar invites the toast chin-chin, while two chins together are a familiar sagging feature of the face

explanation.surface: A round of drinks is called for and everyone raises a glass with the toast chin-chin.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: a large measure of spirits is what you order before the toast 'chin-chin', and 'chin-chin' itself is two chins, the fleshy fold under a plump jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink ordered at twice the standard measure goes by this name, and a second chin under the first is called the same.

clue.text: " Red paper so corrupt " reveals the D.A.

definitions.text: " Red paper so corrupt " reveals the D.A.

parts.note: the Red paper is Pravda, the Soviet Communist daily; the D.A. calls it corrupt, and the word for that is the paper's name with its D A taken away and set between DE and ED

explanation.surface: A district attorney publicly denounces a communist newspaper as crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Pravda, Moscow's Communist ('Red') daily, lies behind the word: write it as DE-PRAVDA-ED and strike out the D.A., and the result means corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone morally corrupted is wicked and debased.

clue.text: Three-horse turnout, fabulous!

definitions.meaning: a carriage drawn by a pair of horses with a third in front
of fable: the one-horned horse of legend is a fabulous beast; adjective standing for the noun

explanation.surface: A three-horse carriage turns out in splendid style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise but means 'of fable': the legendary one-horned horse. A 'turnout' is a horse-drawn equipage, and this name was given to a team of two horses with one leading.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary one-horned horse is the beast of fable, and a pair of horses with a single leader in front bore the same name.

clue.text: Look, a manuscript on hire from, the county

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone spots a manuscript borrowed from the county records.
explanation.walkthrough: Loamshire is a made-up English county, used by George Eliot and later writers as a stand-in for any rural shire. 'on' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Loamshire is a fictional English shire, a stock name for a typical rural county.

clue.text: The land of — and the nurse of arms " (Goldsmith)

parts.note: the gap is filled from Oliver Goldsmith's poem The Traveller, describing Italy as the land of learned men and the nurse of soldiers

explanation.surface: A line of eighteenth-century verse praising a country, with one word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Goldsmith's line runs 'The land of scholars, and the nurse of arms'. The solver needs the poem, or the crossing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith pairs learned men with soldiers, so the blank wants the people of learning that balance 'arms'.

clue.text: On cat lovers in a chatty mood

annotationWithheld.why: On cat lovers in a chatty mood (14): ON CAT LOVERS IN A is an anagram of the answer, but no clue word signals the anagram (an old unflagged anagram), so no op can name an indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: On cat lovers in a chatty mood

clue.text: The end of a love game, perhaps

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps says the word game may be in another form, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Tennis players reach the final point of a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that 'game' may appear in another order. Tennis-minded solvers read 'love game' as a single phrase, but 'love' alone supplies the O. The definition is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a byword for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet stands figuratively for the last of anything, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Islands plus one male

parts.note: plus means and
one is the article a
a male is a man

explanation.surface: A list of islands with one man added.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andaman Islands are an archipelago in the Bay of Bengal belonging to India.

clue.text: Assert this was' the place for an international conference

definitions.text: Assert this was' the place for an international conference

parts.words: Assert this was' the place for an international conference
parts.note: to emphasise is to assert, and the word with its final letter changed to A names Stresa, the Italian lakeside town of the 1935 conference

explanation.surface: Someone insists a certain town once hosted a summit between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Stresa on Lake Maggiore hosted the 1935 conference of Britain, France and Italy; 'this was' says the answer, with its last letter altered to A, was that place.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay emphasis on something is to insist on it firmly, to assert it.

clue.text: Adroit presentation of 'strip-tease in reverse ?

parts.note: a shop's display mannequins are clothed in public view behind glass, the opposite of an undressing act, and skilful display is also a figure for putting a good face on things

explanation.surface: A clever stage show where the performer puts clothes on rather than taking them off.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, clothing mannequins behind a shop's glass front is a striptease run backwards; figuratively the phrase means making something look better than it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging goods attractively in a shop front is skilful display, and the phrase also means putting on a misleadingly good show.

clue.text: Paint Ivor in need

annotationWithheld.why: Paint Ivor in need (9): PAINT IVOR is an anagram of the answer, but the clue as printed has no anagram indicator, so the op cannot name one

clue.text: Beerbohm senior '?

definitions.meaning: the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree points to a tree, and the elderberry is one
older in years or higher in standing

explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree, Max Beerbohm's half-brother, was also the older of the two, so the clue works twice over: his surname leads to a kind of tree, and he was the senior Beerbohm.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's surname Tree suggests a hedgerow tree bearing elderberries, and an older person is the senior one.

clue.text: Rosa due to be wakened

annotationWithheld.why: Rosa due to be wakened (7): ROSA DUE is an anagram of the answer, but the clue as printed has no anagram indicator, so the op cannot name one

clue.text: The great humanist reveals at times a ridiculus little creature !

parts.note: times are periods or ages, eras
Horace wrote that the labouring mountains bring forth a 'ridiculus mus', a ridiculous mouse, and mus is Latin for mouse

explanation.surface: A celebrated scholar of the Renaissance turns out to be a laughable little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'reveals' a link to a hidden word, but none is hidden: it joins definition to wordplay. The Latin tag is from Horace's Ars Poetica, 'parturient montes, nascetur ridiculus mus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading humanist scholar of the Northern Renaissance.

clue.text: The very picture of boredom

parts.note: the clue asks for the single word that sums up weariness and listlessness, as if it were a portrait of tedium

explanation.definitionFit: A French loan word for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, the feeling that nothing is worth doing.

clue.text: There is something charming about the poor doggy's succinct request !

definitions.text: There is something charming about the poor doggy's succinct request !

parts.words: There is something charming about the poor doggy's succinct request
parts.note: a dog's request put in two words is 'want a bone', shortened to a wish and a bone, and the forked chicken bone pulled for luck is a charm

explanation.surface: A hungry dog begs so sweetly that it melts the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means working as a lucky charm: two people pull the forked breastbone of a fowl and the longer piece grants a wish. The dog's short request is 'wish: bone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked breastbone of a bird is pulled apart for luck, the holder of the longer piece making a wish.

clue.text: What an outlandishly offensive expression !

parts.note: a word or usage that offends good taste in language, and 'outlandish' points to the foreign barbarians the word comes from

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a shockingly rude remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlandishly' carries its old sense of foreign: the Greeks called foreigners barbarians, and a usage that offends correct speech is named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrammatical or uncouth word or phrase, felt to be uncivilised use of language, gets this name.

clue.text: Equal to a step up to the defences

parts.note: par means equal, as in on a par

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word step is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A climber reaches the fortifications with one more step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the step, as down clues read from the bottom. 'Equal to' looks like one phrase, but 'to' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parapets are protective walls along the top of a rampart, part of a fort's defences.

clue.text: Aquatic variety of love ?

parts.note: a rearrangement of the word love gives vole, and the river-living vole is commonly given another rodent's name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which kind of love belongs in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of love' rearranges the letters to VOLE; the vole that lives along riverbanks (Ratty in The Wind in the Willows) is popularly called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The European water vole, a riverbank rodent, is widely known by this popular name.

clue.text: Not an improper suggestion from Uncle ?

definitions.text: Not an improper suggestion from Uncle ?

parts.words: Not an improper suggestion from Uncle
parts.note: the pawnbroker is called 'uncle' in old slang, and what he offers is a loan of money, not an unwanted romantic approach

explanation.surface: Someone reassures us that an older relative's proposal was entirely proper.
explanation.walkthrough: An improper suggestion is a romantic or sexual pass, but from 'uncle' the pawnbroker the same word means money lent against a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid ahead of time or lent is called by the same word as a romantic overture.

clue.text: She sends a letter from Greece to the prosecutor

parts.note: rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet
DA is District Attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A woman posts a letter from Greece to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for a woman's name, and 'sends' and 'to' are links joining Greek letter and attorney in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a woman's given name, so it fits a pronoun standing for a female person.

clue.text: Love is on the wing, that's one view

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece being on another means it sits above it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: Love takes flight, so someone says.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures love flying; in fact O (love) sits on top of PINION, a bird's wing. 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief or judgement held by someone is their view of the matter.

clue.text: What a gem of a beetle !

definitions.text: What a gem of a beetle !

parts.words: What a gem of a beetle
parts.note: the sacred dung beetle of Egypt, and also a gemstone cut in that beetle's shape

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lovely little beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gem' is literal: the Egyptians carved precious stones in the shape of this sacred dung beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred dung beetle of ancient Egypt gave its name to engraved stones cut in its shape.

clue.text: There are' thickets of green-hearted lettuce

indicators.note: a lettuce with a green heart has the green word sitting in its middle

parts.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce variety
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Somebody shows us some lettuces with fresh green centres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts the green inside the lettuce. Vert is the heraldic word for green, a crossword staple; 'There are' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverts are patches of undergrowth or small woods where game birds and animals shelter.

clue.text: Complaint that the rum has an explosive content

indicators.note: the explosive is the content held inside the word for the drink

parts.note: taken as written
HE is the military abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the rum is so strong it is practically explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' puts the explosive inside the drink; 'that the' and 'has' are links. HE (high explosive) is a common military abbreviation. The answer is the watery discharge of a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheum is a watery discharge from the nose or eyes, an old word for a cold or catarrh, an ailment.

clue.text: Tuneful little goose !

parts.note: the egg-shaped clay wind instrument takes its name from an Italian word meaning a small goose

explanation.surface: A small gosling honks surprisingly musically.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian name of this clay wind instrument means 'little goose', from its shape; 'tuneful' says it makes music.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument has an Italian name meaning a young goose.

clue.text: Wander over the mountains

definitions.meaning: to roam or move freely over a wide area
a chain of hills or peaks in a line

explanation.surface: A hiker roams over the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam over a wide area is the verb sense, and a line of peaks such as the Andes is the noun sense.

clue.text: Underline order to printer

definitions.meaning: to underline a word in a manuscript
an instruction telling the typesetter to set words in sloping type

explanation.surface: Somebody marks up a page and sends instructions to the print shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a typescript, underlining a word is the conventional instruction to the typesetter to set it in sloping type, so both readings name the same act.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlining in copy tells the typesetter to use sloping type, and that instruction is itself the command to print it slanted.

clue.text: They seem to have a distinct resemblance to Toby!

definitions.text: They seem to have a distinct resemblance to Toby!

parts.words: They seem to have a distinct resemblance to Toby
parts.note: a Toby jug is a pottery drinking vessel shaped like a stout seated man, so ale vessels resemble Toby

explanation.surface: Some people bear an uncanny likeness to a man called Toby.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby is not a person: a Toby jug is a pottery drinking jug moulded as a jolly seated man in a tricorn hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Toby jugs are drinking vessels for ale, so other vessels for drinking ale are their close relatives.

clue.text: Reparation made when morning's over

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
something that is over finishes, it ends

explanation.surface: Someone makes up for a wrong once the morning has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'morning's over' as 'AM ends'; 'made when' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends means making up for a wrong, giving compensation for it.
